documents.title: Academic Integrity: Use of Artificial Intelligence
documents.stance_why: The document sets no AI rule of its own: "If your instructor has established a course-specific policy on AI use, you are expected to follow those guidelines", and absent one students follow the district Standards of Student Conduct and may "consult your instructor". It neither bans nor encourages AI, so it delegates.
documents.summary: De Anza's Academic Senate adopted a short AI paragraph inside the Academic Integrity page. It says AI can help learning but can be misused, defers to each instructor's course policy, falls back on the district conduct standards, and tells unsure students to ask their instructor.

units.why: The senate opens its AI section with a statement that AI "can enhance student learning and support academic success"; this is a principle-setting preamble for the institution, so it is typed as the framework (P56) rather than P44, which is about teaching AI as a professional skill.
units.anchor: can enhance student learning and support academic success

units.why: "AI can also be misused in ways that undermine the learning process" gives the reason for limits on misuse; it is a rationale (informs) and fits P41 (AI shortcuts learning) better than P56 because it names harm to learning.
units.anchor: AI can also be misused in ways that undermine the learning process

units.why: "If your instructor has established a course-specific policy on AI use, you are expected to follow those guidelines" sets no college rule but hands the decision to each instructor; the student "is expected" so modality is must, and P04 fits because the rule is set per instructor.
units.anchor: you are expected to follow those guidelines

units.why: "In the absence of a specific policy, students must use AI tools in accordance with the ... Standards of Student Conduct" states what applies when the course is silent, so P06 (fallback rule) fits; the fallback is the district conduct code, not a ban.
units.anchor: students must use AI tools in accordance with the Foothill-De Anza Community College District
units.policy: In the absence of a specific policy on AI use, students must use AI tools in accordance with the Foothill-De Anza Community College District policy on Standards of Student Conduct.

units.why: "the work submitted represents the students' knowledge and skills" says what the conduct rule means for AI use: submitted work must be the student's own. This is ownership (P29) rather than explain-every-line (P30), since no explanation duty is stated.
units.anchor: when students use AI, the work submitted represents the students’ knowledge and skills
units.policy: When students use AI, the work submitted must represent the students' knowledge and skills.

units.why: "If you are uncertain about appropriate AI use in your coursework, consult your instructor for clarification" directly tells unsure students to ask the instructor, matching P10; modality is should since it is advice.

The integrity section says "It is the responsibility of the faculty to clearly define the requirements and rules applicable to their courses"; not AI-specific but it is the page's general rule that underlies the AI delegation. P09 fits (instructors state rules to students) though it does not mention syllabi or AI by name.
units.anchor: responsibility of the faculty to clearly define the requirements and rules

units.why: "abiding by the rules and regulations set forth by individual faculty members" makes students responsible for following instructor-set rules on assignments and exams, which is the per-instructor rule setting of P04 as applied to students; it is general, not AI-specific.
units.anchor: abiding by the rules and regulations set forth by individual faculty members

units.why: "The submission of work that is not the product of a student's personal effort ... will not be tolerated" is a general ban on submitting work not one's own, which covers AI-produced work in the context of this page; P29 (own what you submit) fits best, and the "will not be tolerated" language is not a penalty (so not P37).
units.anchor: The submission of work that is not the product of a student’s personal effort

units.why: The page quotes Education Code 76130 listing "cheating, plagiarism or knowingly furnishing false information" as misconduct subject to disciplinary sanction; it is a general misconduct classification that frames AI misuse, so P36 fits though AI is not named.
units.anchor: cheating, plagiarism or knowingly furnishing false information in the classroom or to a college officer
units.policy: Cheating, plagiarism or knowingly furnishing false information in the classroom or to a college officer are misconduct for which students are subject to disciplinary sanction.

units.why: "Final authority is determined by the Board of Trustees and district policy documents" says the page is a summary and names the governing board policies (BP 5500, AP 5500, AP 5520); it is a statement of who holds authority over the policy, closest to P56.
units.anchor: Final authority is determined by the Board of Trustees and district policy documents

notes: Single short document. Several units (faculty defining rules, misconduct classification, board authority) are general integrity statements, not AI-specific, coded because they frame the AI paragraph.
